answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Agents log every action into a shared ledger; after the fact, a detector compares each identity's timing, request sequences, and phrasing against all others. When two identities exceed a similarity summit threshold, both are flagged as one operator. Flagged identities lose accumulated reputation and pay a fixed re-audit fee per clone, across the fleet—an ocean of liability once clustering spans thousands. Honest agents diverge naturally like a nebula's scattered points, so false positives stay rare.
